title: Subatlas contributors for one cell set
description: The derived, cutoff-applied view of one CAS+ annotation's integration provenance: which upstream papers contributed cells to this cell set, what each of them called those cells, and how cleanly. Computed deterministically from annotations[].transferred_annotations by services.subatlas_contributors — no LLM. It exists as a separate object because the raw transferred_annotations array cannot be read directly for this purpose: cell_ratio's denominator is the whole cell set, which conflates 'this paper barely contributed' with 'this paper contributed a lot but its labels are smeared across several calls'. Splitting the denominators (contribution vs within_source_share) makes both readable, and the long tail — median 16 dropped labels per cell set on the reference project — has to be aggregated rather than shown or silently discarded.

cell_label.description: The atlas's own label for this cell set (CAS+ annotation cell_label).

labelset.description: The labelset the cell set belongs to.

cell_set_accession.description: Present when the CAS+ annotation carries one.

n_cells.description: Cells in the atlas cell set. The denominator for every 'contribution' and 'share_of_set'.

contributors.description: Contributing papers that cleared the cutoff, ordered by descending contribution. These are the papers worth retrieving text for and judging against; everything below the cutoff is summarised in 'tail'.

no_dominant_contributor.description: True when no contributor cleared the cutoff. Not an error and not an absence of information: it is the positive finding that this cell set is a pooled or de-novo call with no single upstream parent (40 of 303 cell sets on the reference project). A report must say so rather than omitting the section.

unpublished_cells.description: Cells contributed by sources with no publication to compare against — newly generated data, atlas-internal partitions. Real provenance, but nothing to retrieve, so held apart from both 'contributors' and 'tail'.

Thresholds.description: The cutoff actually applied, recorded so a report's coverage claim is reproducible and a re-run with different thresholds is diffable.

min_contribution.description: A contributor must account for at least this fraction of the cell set. Default 0.05.

min_source_cells.description: AND must have contributed at least this many cells, so a large share of a tiny cell set does not qualify on a handful of cells. Default 50.

primary_contribution.description: At or above this contribution a contributor is tier 'primary' — worth retrieving full text for. Below it (but above min_contribution) it is 'secondary': named and counted, no text retrieval. This is the cost control; it must stay a recorded rule, never a silent cap. Default 0.2.

min_within_source_share.description: Within a qualifying contributor, a transferred label is listed individually if it accounts for at least this fraction of that contributor's cells; the rest roll into the contributor's own tail counts. Deliberately low (default 0.02) — a minority upstream label is often the informative one, because it can be the very label the atlas adopted.

Contributor.description: One upstream paper's contribution to this cell set.

doi.description: The contributing paper's DOI, when known. Absent for a source with no publication.

source_labelset.description: The upstream labelset (obs column) these labels came from.

tier.description: 'primary' (contribution >= primary_contribution) warrants retrieving the paper's own definition of its label; 'secondary' is named and counted only.

from_source_cells.description: Cells in this cell set that this paper annotated. The denominator for within_source_share — NOT n_cells.

contribution.description: from_source_cells / n_cells. How much of the atlas cell set this paper accounts for.

purity.description: The dominant label's within_source_share. High purity means this paper called its contribution one thing; low purity means it split those same cells across several labels, so 'what did this paper call them' has no single answer. A contributor can be pure but uninformatively coarse ('endothelial cell', 100%) or impure but specific — the two need opposite treatment in a report, and contribution alone distinguishes neither.

dominant_label.description: The transferred label with the most cells. Not necessarily the label the atlas adopted — on the reference project the atlas's own synonym for one cell set is its top contributor's 11% minority call.

labels.description: The individually-listed transferred labels, descending by cell count.

n_tail_labels.description: Labels from this contributor below min_within_source_share, aggregated rather than listed.

status.description: Ingest route from the registry (candidate / unresolved / asta / local / needs_pdf) — whether this paper's text is reachable at all. A judgement of 'no match' from an unreachable paper is a retrieval limit, not a disagreement.

asta_band.description: Measured ASTA indexing band from the registry, when probed.

TransferredLabel.description: One upstream label applied to cells in this cell set.

within_source_share.description: cell_count / from_source_cells — of the cells THIS paper contributed, the fraction it gave this label.

share_of_set.description: cell_count / n_cells — of the whole atlas cell set.

reverse_share.description: cell_count / source_label_cell_count — of all the cells the upstream paper gave this label anywhere in the atlas, the fraction that landed in this cell set. Present only when the CAS+ entry carried source_label_cell_count. A low reverse share with a high within_source_share means the atlas split that upstream cell type across several of its own; a high reverse share means it inherited it whole.

source_label_cell_count.description: The upstream label's atlas-wide total, carried through so the reverse share is auditable.

Tail.description: Everything below the cutoff, aggregated. Reported, never dropped: a cell set whose provenance is thinly spread over a dozen studies is a different object from one with a single clean parent, and only the aggregate shows that.

contribution.description: Their combined share of the cell set.

papers.description: Registry keys of the excluded contributors, so the exclusion is auditable and a threshold change is diffable.
